reason: The week-12 international-broadening book filled on 2026-10-05, four sessions ago. Every leg is within noise of entry (TLT short -1.1%, DXJ -0.7%, EFV -0.5%, KIE +0.9%, VWO -1.4%, VEA -1.1%). The largest drawdown, EUAD at -4.0%, is far from its 15% stop. Research was limited. Three web searches gave partial, partly contradictory coverage of Oct 2-7 and nothing for the Oct 9 close, and recap pages I tried to fetch were refused (403/503). What I did find is relevant to the biggest leg, the TLT short. Reports had the 10-year touching roughly 5.36% midweek and the 30-year near 5.28%, multi-decade highs, even though Treasury expanded its long-end buyback program to $4bn per operation. That supports the term-premium and deficit-supply thesis, but it also shows an active official backstop on the long end. TLT nonetheless closed the week only 1.1% above my entry, so the 10% stop and 20% take-profit already bound the risk sensibly. Soft US payrolls (+29k) cut Fed-hike odds, which fits the weaker-dollar premise behind VWO/VEA/EFV. Oil back above $100 on Hormuz is a headwind for importers like Japan and Europe, but not yet enough to justify churning a four-day-old book. Holding also leaves the Round 2/Round 3 overlap unchanged at zero shared symbols, so the novelty rule is still satisfied.
